Compute the remainder when \( S \) is divided by 2027. (Note that 2027 is prime.)

message.content:
Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). Work modulo \(p\).

Define

\[
F(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \binom{2k}{k}x^k.
\]

Then

\[
S=\left. xF'(x)\right|_{x=2}=2F'(2).
\]

We claim that

\[
F(x)\equiv (1-4x)^m \pmod p.
\]

Indeed, by Lucas’ theorem, for \(k>m\),

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p.
\]

For \(0\le k\le m\), since \(m\equiv -\frac12\pmod p\),

\[
\binom{m}{k}(-4)^k
\equiv \binom{2k}{k}\pmod p.
\]

Thus the coefficients match, giving \(F(x)\equiv(1-4x)^m\).

Therefore

\[
F'(x)=-4m(1-4x)^{m-1},
\]

so

\[
S=2F'(2)\equiv -8m(1-8)^{m-1}\pmod p.
\]

Since \(-8m=-4(p-1)\equiv 4\pmod p\), we get

\[
S\equiv 4(-7)^{1012}\equiv 4\cdot 7^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

By Euler’s criterion,

\[
7^{1013}\equiv \left(\frac{7}{2027}\right).
\]

Quadratic reciprocity gives

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=(-1)^{3\cdot 1013}\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
=-1\cdot 1=-1.
\]

Hence

\[
7^{1012}\equiv -7^{-1}\pmod{2027},
\]

and so

\[
S\equiv -4\cdot 7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Finally,

\[
7(-289)=-2023\equiv 4\pmod{2027},
\]

so \(4\cdot 7^{-1}\equiv -289\). Therefore

\[
S\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
